blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre neurociência a partir da transcrição de uma palestra, explicando conceitos complexos com analogias e ressalvas.

body: Esta aula treina **ouvir e anotar informações (IELTS Listening, TOEFL Listening)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Lecture: How Memory Is Consolidated
paras: Professor: Let’s start with a common misconception: memories are not stored like files. **Rather**, they are **reconstructed** each time we recall them. During sleep, the **hippocampus** replays the day’s experiences, **gradually transferring** them to the **cortex**, a process called **consolidation**.

**Think of it as** a librarian shelving books overnight. **Of course**, the analogy has limits: shelved books do not change, but **memories do**. **So what follows?** That vivid recall is **not necessarily accurate recall**, and that **sleep matters**.

items.q: Sleep helps transfer memories to the cortex.

blocks.body: Boas explicações têm: **mito → modelo → analogia → limite da analogia → consequência**. Em exames, ouça as **ressalvas**: costumam ser a resposta.

items.s: Memories are ___ each time we recall them. (reconstruct, part.)
Think ___ it as a librarian shelving books. (of)
Vivid recall is not necessarily ___ recall. (accurate)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.pt: A analogia do bibliotecário é exata?

body: **Slip one’s mind.** — Esquecer.
**Ring a bell.** — Soar familiar.
**Rack one’s brains.** — Quebrar a cabeça.
**Learn by heart.** — Decorar.
**Etched in memory.** — Gravado na memória.
**On the tip of my tongue.** — Na ponta da língua.
**Jog someone’s memory.** — Refrescar a memória.
**A trip down memory lane.** — Uma viagem à memória.
**In the back of my mind.** — No fundo da minha mente.
**Sleep on it.** — Pensar com calma.
**Are memories stored like files?** — Memórias são guardadas como arquivos?
**No, that’s a misconception. They’re reconstructed.** — Não, é um equívoco. São reconstruídas.
**Is the librarian analogy accurate?** — A analogia do bibliotecário é exata?

blocks.title: After class
lines: No, that’s a misconception. They’re reconstructed.

A analogia do bibliotecário é exata?
Partly. Books don’t change; memories do.
Em parte. Livros não mudam; memórias sim.

items.label: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances
items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

prompts.model: Think of it as a librarian shelving books.
Of course, memories change while books don’t.

blocks.task: Write a 5-sentence explanation of a scientific idea with a misconception, an analogy and its limit.
blocks.model: A common misconception is that the immune system works like a wall. Rather, it is more like a patrol that learns to recognise threats. Think of it as a security team with a growing photo album of intruders. Of course, the analogy has limits: it does not capture how cells communicate. The practical consequence is that vaccines train the patrol.
